title: Intranasal application of immuno-regulatory molecules: a method to investigate strategies for local cancer immuno-therapies in the lung
protocol: Intravenously inject 2x10^5 tumour cells per mouse in the tail vein for L1C2 adenocarcinoma induction using Balbc/J mice or C57BL/6 mice for B16-F10 melanoma induction.
Embed lung tissue in paraffin and cut into 4 micrometer thick sections.
Stain sections with Hematoxylin/Eosin (H&E) according to standardized histological protocols.
Prepare the cell culture media DMEM with 10% FCS and 1% penicillin/streptomycin for B16F10 cells, and RPMI with 10% FCS and 1% penicillin/streptomycin for L1C2 cells.
Store the prepared cell culture media at 4°C.
Warm the stored cell culture media to 37°C.
Transfer frozen tumour cells from liquid nitrogen into a tube.
Dissolve the thawed cells using the warm media.
Centrifuge the cells at 91g (800rpm) for 7 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 10 ml of media.
Culture the cells in a 50ml culture flask until they reach 70-80% confluency.
Remove the culture media from the cells when ready to split them.
Wash the cells with 10 ml of PBS.
Pipette accutase into the flask based on the size of the flask (0.5 ml for 25 cm², 1 ml for 75 cm², and 2 ml for 175 cm²).
Incubate the accutase with the cells for 1-2 minutes at 37°C.
Beat the flask to detach the cells from the surface.
Apply 10 ml of media to stop the accutase reaction.
Transfer the cell suspension into a tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 91g (800rpm) for 7 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in media.
Cultivate and expand the cells in a 75 cm² or 175 cm² flask.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 10 ml media.
Mix 10 µl of the cell suspension with 10 µl trypan blue.
Fill 10 µl of the mix into the chamber and count cells in four squares (Q1-Q4).
Calculate the cell number as follows: (Q1 + Q2 + Q3 + Q4)/4 x 2 x 10^4 = cell number/ml cell suspension.
Transfer the calculated cell volume (2x10^5 cells per mouse) into a tube and centrifuge at 91g for 7 min, 4°C.
Resuspend B16-F10 cells in sterofundin or RPMI to achieve a concentration of 1x10^6 cells/ml (200 µl/ 2x10^5 cells will be injected into the mouse).
Prepare an Erlenmeyer flask with hand-warm water.
Fix the mouse in the injection chamber and place the tail into the Erlenmeyer flask for 30 seconds.
Alternatively, warm the tail using an infrared lamp.
Take up 200 µl cell suspension in the syringe.
Insert the syringe horizontally into the tail vein of the mouse and inject the cell suspension slowly.
Prepare the solution for intranasal treatment and store it on ice.
Dissolve 1 g of 2,2,2-Tribromo-Ethanol in 1 ml t-Amyl-Alcohol.
Ad 39 ml PBS and vortex until total dissolving.
Store the avertin solution protected from light at 4°C.
Mix ketamin (12 mg/ml) with xylazin (0.08 ml/ml) in PBS and store at 4°C.
Anesthetize the mice using one of the following methods:
Inject 200 µl avertin intraperitoneally into the mice.
Inject 60-70 µl ketamin intraperitoneally into the mice.
Use the isoflurane system according to manufacturer's instructions.
Put the mice in the plastic chamber.
Anesthetize the mice by flooding the box with isoflurane/oxygen.
Increase the doses of isoflurane slowly.
Clamp the mouse in the neck and tilt the head back when the mouse is immobilized and the heart beat is getting slower.
Pipette the solution carefully, drop-wise into the nose of the mouse so that the mouse inhales the solution.
Wait until the mouse wakes up.
Warm the mouse with an infrared lamp until it is awake.
